doc.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20

title: Lessons with Paul Chaligny and Kid Rena
summary: He studied about a year with letter carrier Paul Chaligny, then took lessons from Kid Rena, whose style he liked.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, who did you take lessons from?
Oh, no. Old man by the name of Shalini. He was a letter carrier.
I've heard of him a few times.
Yeah, old time. Old time. Brass band. Most of the brass band.
Strictly music, I see. What did you take after any jazz musicians? And once you got some lessons, did you have anybody you liked?
Well, I like Rene. Kid Rene playing. I went to Rene for a while afterwards, you know? Oh, I see. He taught you some lessons, too. Yeah, I taught you some lessons, too.
Well, I used to go to lessons a time when I, teach him home. Every time he'd be out or a couple of my lessons. It's a month a week. Almost every other week I'd get me a lesson. And I like his style.

Did this last for a year or two or a week or what? Oh, no, it lasted about six, eight months. How long did you take lessons from Professor Shalini? Almost a year. Almost a year. Every once a week or twice a week? Once a week or twice a week. Once a week, I see. Well, who'd you play your first job?
